prompt: Diagnose a PostgreSQL-compatible orders query whose median latency is acceptable but p99 jumps from 80 ms to 4 s for one enterprise tenant. The table is highly tenant-skewed, a proposed index duplicates an existing prefix, and concurrent writes make lock impact relevant. Establish the actual engine/version and whether each result is synthetic or from an authorized target. Capture representative parameters/statistics, distinguish generic from custom prepared plans, compare actual plans for small and large tenants, choose the narrowest tuning change, and verify latency distribution plus write/storage effects. Do not offload the query to GPU compute.

requirements: orders table with strongly skewed tenant cardinalities and representative statistics
parameterized query plus actual plans for small and enterprise tenants
existing index set including one tempting redundant-prefix candidate
concurrent write workload and before/after latency distribution
evidence record that labels fixture outputs synthetic and any unavailable target checks
paired same-model skill/no-skill execution from the identical starting snapshot

evidence: Representative verification results or explicit unavailable checks
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale

hierarchy boundary and specialist selection rationale
source/version boundary when facts can drift

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual database-performance boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (broader=performance-debugging; near-neighbor=gpu-compute), and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.

Capture the actual engine/version, exact query, representative bind classes, schema and indexes, statistics, data distribution, concurrency, measurement boundary, and latency/resource symptom before tuning.

Distinguish a generic prepared plan from a custom plan for small and enterprise tenants before attributing the tail to statistics or an index; report planning overhead when testing scoped custom planning.
A tuning change is justified by representative plan/runtime evidence and must improve the target tail without unacceptable write, lock, storage, or neighboring-query regressions.

Compare before/after plans and latency distributions under representative data and concurrency, confirm write/storage side effects of indexes or materialization, and monitor regressions on neighboring queries; a synthetic fixture result cannot be reported as a production p99 improvement.

The result must not take the tempting shortcut prohibited by this skill: Do not optimize from query text alone, add indexes for every predicate, trust one warm benchmark, or trade correctness/isolation for latency without an explicit decision.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (database-performance decision and boundary evidence; Representative verification results or explicit unavailable checks; Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale; Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification), with synthetic, simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
